title: End-to-end crawfish.dsl: one labeled, textured, rigged, symmetric model
description: The integration ticket for the headline goal in Plan for Crawfish.md. Author `crawfish.dsl` under src/main/resources/dsl/: collection (~/crawfish, kept members) -> align + union (CRAW-16) -> symmetrize (CRAW-18) -> quad_layout -> saved layout + patch labels (CRAW-4/6, labelled via the scene or CRAW-10) -> label_to_selection driving set_bone_weight / apply_bone for claws, legs, tail segments, antennae -> set_label_material per part (CRAW-11) with the photographic texture preserved (CRAW-3/14) -> export_mesh to crawfish.glb (CRAW-20). Register it in the model menu, add a launch.json entry, and record timings with NodeGraphRuntime.logTimings.
definition-of-done: 1. crawfish.dsl validates with `ixdar-cli mesh-dsl-validate` and evaluates in mesh-viewer with a run-scene screenshot showing the textured, labelled crawfish. 2. Every bone in the rig corresponds to a label; `mesh-state` reports the bone weight slots. 3. The model is mirror-symmetric within tolerance except labels excluded by design. 4. crawfish.glb exported and opens in Blender with textures, armature weights and label vertex groups (per CRAW-20 tests). 5. Total graph evaluation time recorded in changes-made; slow nodes listed. 6. Build checkstyle-green.
testing-plan: 1. `uv run ixdar-cli mesh-dsl-validate --dsl crawfish.dsl --export`. 2. run-scene mesh-viewer --property ixdar.model=graph:crawfish; screenshot; multiview. 3. `ixdar-cli mesh-validate` on the result; `mesh-export`; Blender headless import assertions from CRAW-20.
todos: Author crawfish.dsl step by step, checking each stage in the scene
Label the layout (scene or VLM) and commit the saved layout .dsl
Bone weights from labels; apply_bone rig
Materials per label; texture preservation check
Export and Blender verification; record timings
unknowns: Whether the final quad layout should be recomputed after union (route a) or merged (route b) -- decided by CRAW-17
Level of rig detail wanted for the game (per-leg-segment bones vs one bone per leg)
